audit.why: 38.6% over 57 games — the worst matchup in this slice by a wide margin, and the recorded sides say why: Aurora holds only level 1 and level 6, Fiora owns 3-5 and both item stages. Lunge falls from 13s to 6s across its ranks while Across the Veil only goes 22s to 18s, so her ability to re-close outpaces your ability to leave.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named her ultimate "Between the Worlds" and gave no ultimate cooldowns.
audit.why: Grand Challenge is 110/90/70 against Between Worlds' 140/120/100 — hers is 30 seconds cheaper at every rank, and on a completed vital chain it heals her and every ally nearby. Trading ultimates at 6 loses on cooldown and on payoff.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones her all-in, but Grand Challenge is 110s and heals her whole side on a full vital chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text, wants.you[2], mid and whys[4] all rest the level-6 plan on Between Worlds making Aurora untargetable to Fiora. It does not. Separately, Riposte's stun condition is stated as though it always stuns, when Riot's text makes the stun conditional.
audit.why: Riposte (W, 24/22/20/18/16, 750): 'parries all incoming damage and disables for a short time, then stabs in a direction. This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' Against Aurora specifically that distinction matters: The Weirding applies a slow, and a slow is not an immobilizing effect, so poking into a raised Riposte gets you slowed rather than stunned. The genuine danger is a jungler's hard CC landing into it. Riposte at 24s at rank 1 is also the longest cooldown in either kit — that is the window, and it is 8 seconds longer than her rank-5 Lunge. Duelist's Dance (P) heals her on every vital hit and Grand Challenge heals her allies too, so Grievous Wounds is not optional here. Lunge applies on-hit effects, which is why her damage scales with attack speed rather than reading as flat ability damage.
audit.corrected: Riposte only stuns if it parries an immobilize — your E slow makes it a slow, so the stun risk is your jungler's CC.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is correctly named as the tracked cooldown but never given a number.
audit.why: 24s at rank 1 against a 13s Lunge means the parry is down for roughly eleven seconds of every cycle at level 3, and that gap closes to nine by rank 5. It is the only clock in this lane worth counting.
audit.corrected: Riposte is 24s at rank 1 — bait it, then you have a real window before Lunge is back.

audit.why: breakdown.late already carries anti-heal as core, which is right — Duelist's Dance heals on every vital and Grand Challenge heals her team. Naming the sources is the improvement.

notes: The Riposte stun is conditional in Riot's text — it stuns only if Fiora parried an immobilizing effect — and The Weirding applies a slow, not an immobilize. The page presents the stun as automatic, which makes players refuse a trade they can actually take. What genuinely creates the stun is your own jungler's hard CC landing into a raised parry, so the coordination note matters more than the trading note. The 'mid' paragraph still carries the untargetability claim and needs a later rewrite.
